title: NimbleBrain Host Extension
description: Schema for the `ai.nimblebrain/host` MCP `_meta` extension — how an MCP server declares its UI integration (placements, briefing, notifications) in the NimbleBrain host shell. Carried in the server's descriptor `_meta`, which for this host is the connector catalog's ServerDetail entry. The `ui://` app resources themselves are standard MCP Apps; this extension only declares where they are placed.

host_version.description: Host extension contract version. Known values: "1.0", "1.1" (introduced a host_capabilities block the host no longer reads), "1.2" (adds hooks), "1.3" (adds notifications). FORWARD-COMPATIBLE, and this tolerance is part of the contract: an unknown version is NOT rejected — the host parses the fields it understands and ignores the rest; unknown top-level keys validate and are ignored; an unknown or malformed placement slot drops only that placement, never the whole declaration. The version-to-block pairing is advisory and is not schema-enforced.

name.description: Display name shown in the sidebar and app list.

category.description: RESERVED — not currently consumed by the host (grouping/briefing prioritization is not yet wired to it). Free-form string, tolerated for back-compat; do not rely on it. Slated for removal — see nimblebrain#503.

resourceUri.description: ui:// URI for the main view.

hooks.description: Inbound event streams this server accepts, one entry per vendor. READ FROM A CATALOG CONNECTOR ONLY — the host resolves hooks from the operator-published connector catalog, never from an MCPB bundle manifest, because the route and registration tool decide where a delivery is sent and must come from operator-trusted metadata. Declaring hooks in an MCPB manifest has no effect. The host mints a capability URL per (workspace, connector, vendor) when the server is installed, hands it to the declared register_tool, and forwards deliveries to that URL verbatim to the declared route on this same server — body bytes unchanged, the vendor's own headers passed through. The host never parses a delivery body: signature verification, parsing, idempotency and state are entirely the server's. Declare host_version "1.2" alongside this block.

HookDeclaration.description: One inbound event stream. This is the entire vendor-specific configuration the host ever sees — a name, a route, a tool, and prose. It deliberately cannot describe payload shapes or event taxonomies.

vendor.description: Vendor slug, lowercase alphanumeric with internal hyphens. Appears as a path segment in the minted URL and is sealed into its token, so the two are cross-checked on every delivery. One entry per vendor: a duplicate is dropped.

route.description: Absolute path ON THIS SERVER that a delivery is forwarded to, e.g. "/ingest/acme". Resolved against this server's own base URL and refused if it resolves to a different origin, so it may not be protocol-relative ("//host"), contain "..", a backslash, a fragment, or control characters.

register_tool.description: Name of a tool on THIS server that the host calls with { vendor, url } — both strings — to hand over the minted URL. The tool must exist on the server's tools/list at install time AND accept those two arguments. If it does not, no URL is minted for any of this server's streams and the operator is shown a warning naming the declaration — the connector still installs and its tools still work. The check re-runs whenever the connection is re-established, so fixing the manifest and reconnecting provisions the streams without a reinstall. Typically the server stores the URL in its own operator-writable config and registers it with the vendor.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this stream carries. Operator-facing only — the host never acts on it.

header_renames.description: Rename inbound headers before the forward, as { from: to }. The forward strips the header class a caller could use to assert identity (authorization, x-api-key, x-tenant-id, x-workspace-id, …) — the same class the fleet edge strips. A vendor that authenticates its deliveries on one of those headers cannot otherwise reach its own verifier, so declaring a rename moves the value to a header the strip list does not cover. A rename whose target is itself in the stripped class is ignored.

NotificationsDeclaration.description: The outbox this server exposes — one MCP resource the host reads on a schedule for facts nobody asked for (a domain went active, a reply landed). The host reads it as the RFC 6570 template <resource>{?cursor,maxEvents,maxAgeMs} and expects the MCP Triggers-and-Events poll result { events, cursor, truncated, hasMore, nextPollMs }. Declaring an outbox grants NO privilege: nothing is minted, no new token audience exists, and no path to a human is opened — a workspace admin's route does that. What it does impose is cost, a standing poll per (workspace, connector), which the host bounds with its own cadence floor, backoff and per-workspace budget. Declare host_version "1.3" alongside this block.

resource.description: The outbox resource URI, e.g. "acme://notifications". Scheme and path are both the server's own. Three rules bind. It must carry a scheme. It must NOT carry a query string or a fragment, because the host appends {?cursor,maxEvents,maxAgeMs} itself and a server-supplied query would either be overwritten or produce two. And its scheme must not be one the host resolves itself — skill://, ui://, instructions://, artifact://, files://, app:// — because a single resource cannot mean two things to the same reader; such a declaration is refused and the outbox is never polled.

description.description: What the outbox carries. Operator-facing only — the host never acts on it.

slot.description: Shell slot to fill: "sidebar" (core nav), "sidebar.<group>" (named group, e.g. "sidebar.apps"), "sidebar.bottom" (pinned), "settings" (a settings section — declare settings as a placement, not a separate object), or "main" (page content). Unknown slots are dropped by the host, never fatal.

resourceUri.description: ui:// resource URI served by this MCP server.

priority.description: Sort order within the slot. Lower values appear first. Default: 100.

label.description: Human-readable label for sidebar items and tabs.

size.description: Size hint for the slot renderer.

BriefingBlock.description: Briefing declaration — how this app contributes to the daily briefing.

priority.description: Relative priority for ordering this app's facets in the briefing.

facets.description: Summary dimensions this app contributes to the briefing.

BriefingFacet.description: One dimension of a server's briefing contribution. Resolved via exactly one of `resource` (an MCP resource read) or `tool` (an MCP tool call) — both answered by the server that declared the facet. The host never reads a server's data itself, so there is no host-side query. A facet declaring neither falls back to `description`.

label.description: Human-readable label for the briefing section.

type.description: Facet type: attention (needs action), upcoming (coming soon), activity (happened), delta (state change), kpi (headline number).

resource.description: URI of an MCP resource on this server that returns the facet's summary.

tool.description: Name of an MCP tool on this server to call at briefing time.

tool_input.description: Arguments to pass when calling the tool (e.g., { "query": "AI", "page_size": 5 }).

description.description: Human-readable fallback description of what this facet shows.
